newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sells Lensvyaz telecom stake over market.
newsitem.headline: Russia sells Lensvyaz telecom stake over market.

text.p: A two percent stake in northwest Russian telecom Lensvyaz was sold for 20.92 billion roubles ($3.6 million), about twice the starting price, at an auction on Thursday, a Leningrad region property fund official said.

"All the lots were bought by one buyer -- a Russian legal entity," said auction specialist Lyudmila Kalashnikova. "The packet was sold for 20.92 billion roubles on a starting price of 11.668 billion," she said.
The price was also higher than that on the RTS-2 market of less liquid shares where it was last quoted on Wednesday at $56.50/$59.00 bid/offer.
Kalashnikova declined to name the winner of the auction, at which there were 21 bids for 53,038 ordinary shares of AO Lensvyaz, sold in 10 lots.

The two-percent stake is part of 22 percent of company shares returned to the Leningrad regional property fund by an investor which won an investment tender but did not fulfil conditions of the agreement.
Lensvyaz, located in the region around St Petersburg, had pretax profit of 67.5 billion roubles in 1996 after 41 billion in 1995 to Russian accounting standards on an accruals basis.
Svyazinvest holding company owns a 38 percent stake which is a majority of voting shares.
